page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.large is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by a single physical core through hyper-threading on the x86_64 architecture. Memory is allocated at 8.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent volumes, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. System virtualization is managed via KVM, with hardware instruction support including AVX-512F and AES-NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level compute and memory bandwidth characteristics consistent with legacy hardware generations. In raw CPU testing, the server recorded a single-core stress-ng score of 1099.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0, placing it within the lower performance tiers. Multi-core results, including PassMark CPU (1826.13) and Geekbench multi-core (1108.0), reflect the throughput limitations of a single physical core. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 10.45 GB/s, while write operations measured 9.47 GB/s. Application testing demonstrated 1.48 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.26 GB/s of static web serving throughput.

The ecs.g5ne.large functions as an economical dedicated resource profile where low execution costs and predictable allocation take precedence over raw speed. The primary architectural constraint is the shared-core execution model inherent in having only one physical core for two vCPUs, which bounds parallel performance and intensive I/O tasks. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for low-traffic web applications, non-critical background jobs, lightweight staging environments, and basic internal microservices.
